chunks: Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام was asked about a man from whom these people take the zakat of his wealth, or the khums of his spoils, or the khums of what is extracted for him from the mines: is that counted for him toward his zakat and khums?

key_terms.أَيُحْسَبُ: is it counted; whether it is legally recognized toward the obligation
key_terms.الْمَعَادِنِ: the mines; mineral resources extracted from the earth
key_terms.خُمُسَ: khums; the one-fifth due on specified categories of wealth
key_terms.زَكَاةَ: zakat; the obligatory alms due on qualifying wealth
key_terms.غَنِيمَتِهِ: his spoils; gains upon which khums may be due

ai.seo_question: If zakat or khums is taken from a person by the authorities, does it count as fulfillment of his obligation?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that if zakat or khums is taken from a person by the authorities mentioned in the report, it is counted for that person as fulfillment of his zakat and khums obligation. The narration concerns financial duties in Shia fiqh, specifically zakat, khums on ghanimah, and khums on mineral extraction.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.1656 - Abu al-Hasan (Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim (as)) was asked about a man from whom others take the Zakat of his wealth, the Khums of his spoils, or the Khums of what he extracts from the mines:
"Is that counted for him as fulfilling his Zakat and Khums obligations?"
